heading: Revamping History: Redesigning the Blinken OSA Archivum's Visual Identity and Website

blocks.label: Overview
paragraphs: The Blinken OSA Archivum, located in Budapest, is a multifaceted archival institution housing significant collections and historical documents. Its focus is primarily on the history and aftermath of the Cold War, severe international human rights violations, and marginalized communities. In 2024, I collaborated with Studio Stoki to contribute to the visual identity for the Archivum and completely overhauled their website, which included creating a comprehensive design system as part of the process.

blocks.label: The problem
paragraphs: Visitors couldn’t find what they came for. The Archivum serves very different people, from researchers looking for a specific collection to the public checking an exhibition or an event. The old navigation didn’t reflect any of them: everything competed at the same level, so the site worked for no one in particular. The task wasn’t a visual refresh. It was deciding who the site is for, and making that visible in its structure.

blocks.label: The process
paragraphs: I started with a persona workshop with the Archivum’s stakeholders, which surfaced their different views of who the “main” user was and gave us four personas to check every decision against. The biggest challenge came right here: I couldn’t interview the people who actually use the archive, and those insights were painfully missing. So I treated the personas as assumptions to test rather than facts, leaned on the staff who work with researchers and visitors every day, and validated the structure before any visual design began.

From the personas I rebuilt the information architecture around what each audience comes to do, instead of how the Archivum is organised internally. I chose fewer, clearer top-level paths and let depth live inside the sections, accepting that some content would sit one click further away. I then turned the structure into detailed wireframes and clickable prototypes, and walked through them with the Archivum’s team while changes were still cheap.

For the final UI, I worked closely with Studio Stoki so the identity and the website grew as one system: the brand leads in typography and key moments, while quiet layouts let the archival material speak. Alongside the screens I built a design system of reusable components and templates, so the team can keep publishing without needing a designer for every new page.

blocks.label: The outcome
paragraphs: The new site gives each of the Archivum’s audiences a clear route to what they’re looking for, and a design system that lets the team keep publishing in a consistent way. The project, together with the new visual identity, received an RGB Award.
